text: part. Before we compared the model to the experimental results, we examined the PCC properties, which have a large impact on the device performance. First, we changed the density from 836 to 872 kg m-3 to match the volume and mass of the uncycled slab. We then looked at the surface temperature probes and compared the measurements to our expectations. Initially we assumed that the graphite/tetradecane had a transition temperature of 4.6°C and a temperature glide of 0.5°C based on earlier DSC measurements. The phase change temperatures can be identified by examining the surface thermocouple measurements between the PCC and insulation (Figure 18a) since the heat flows through the top surface are minimal. Here the phase change endset temperature is closer to 6°C than the originally assumed 4.85°C. We investigated these values further with temperature-history experiments with tetradecane. These experiments found that the transition temperature and temperature glide were closer to 5.4°C and 1°C, respectively. The comparison between the modeled and measured PCC surface temperatures are shown in Figure 18. We adjusted the model values to account for the fact that the sensors we placed on the outside of the Mylar encapsulation. The trends are similar between the model and the experiment, although the PCC temperature drops more quickly near the insulation surface. This may be due to differences in the PCC properties (not as sharp of a transition at the onset point). Figure 18: The measured PCC temperatures at the surface (a) between the PCC and the insulation and (b) between the PCC and the microchannel wall when the average charge rate is 325 W and the discharge rate is 160 W. The model was then compared to the experimental data for a range of discharge rates. The results are shown in Figure 19. The model results align well with the experimental data, showing both the correct trends and temperature values. The absolute average deviation for the discharge and charge circuit outlet temperatures were 0.27 and 0.29°C, respectively. This shows that the model can accurately predict the outlet states of the fluid. Comparison to Previous Design With the validated model, we were able to compare the microchannel design to the experimental data collected with the glycol-coupled serpentine component (Goyal et al., 2021). The capacity in the model was set to match the serpentine component, and the flow rates and temperature differences across each fluid stream were set to match the experimental targets.
